en-US.longDescription:
Redefining the open-source download manager

Design & Motion
Every transition and micro-interaction has been carefully tuned to follow Material Design 3 motion guidelines:
- Asymmetric timing — enter animations are slightly longer than exits, giving new content time to land while dismissed content leaves quickly
- Emphasized easing curves — decelerate on enter (cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1)), accelerate on exit (cubic-bezier(0.3, 0, 0.8, 0.15)), replacing generic ease curves throughout the codebase
- Spring-based modals — dialogs use physically-modeled spring animations for a natural, responsive feel
- Consistent motion tokens — all durations and curves are defined as CSS custom properties, ensuring a unified rhythm across 12+ components

Features
- Multi-protocol downloads — HTTP, HTTPS, SFTP, ED2K, BitTorrent, Magnet, and .torrent tasks
- HLS and DASH — Native track selection, subtitles, live recording, resumable media downloads and MP4/MKV output. See media downloads.
- BitTorrent — Selective file download, DHT, peer exchange, encryption controls, metadata caching, GeoIP peer flags, and tracker probing
- Browser extension integration — Embedded Extension API with independent authentication, download confirmation, smart auto-submit, filename hints, referer/cookie forwarding, and real-time controls (Rayburst Connect)
- Safe filename handling — Content-Disposition, RFC 2047, non-UTF-8, percent-encoded, and extensionless URL resolution with path traversal sanitization
- Download organization — Favorite and recent folders, optional file-type categorization, stale-record cleanup, and completed history backed by SQLite
- Concurrent downloads — Independent limits for active tasks, stream connections, and BitTorrent peers
- Speed control — Global and per-task upload/download limits with day-of-week and time-of-day scheduling
- System integration — Tray operation, optional tray speed display, macOS Dock badge/progress, protocol handlers for magnet://, ed2k://, thunder://, and rayburst://
- Lightweight mode — Destroys the WebView on minimize-to-tray while Rust keeps the engine, task monitor, notifications, history, and extension routing alive
- Notifications and power options — Native task start/complete/failure notifications, keep-awake during downloads, and optional shutdown after completion
- Network controls — Scoped proxy support for downloads, app updates, and tracker updates, plus system proxy detection
- Auto-update channels — Stable, Beta, and Latest Across Channels policies with separate download and install phases
- Diagnostics — Structured logs, exportable diagnostic ZIPs, database integrity checks and Linux GPU rendering fallback
- Personalization — Light/dark/system theme, 10 color schemes, 27 languages, and first-launch system language detection
- Native desktop app — Tauri 2 with a Rust backend
en-US.name: Rayburst
en-US.releaseNotes:
What's Changed
This release collects the 4.1.2 betas. Rayburst uses far less CPU and memory, both while downloading and while it sits in the tray. The proxy can follow the system, links copied in other apps can open the add window, and the app's own downloads go through the engine. It bundles Aria2 Next 3.1.0 and fixes the app freezing when quitting from the tray.
✨ New Features
- Follow the system proxy — the new "System" proxy source uses the proxy the OS names when each download starts, and for the app's own requests. When the browser keeps a download because the engine could not reach it, a notification says why (#784)
- Background clipboard watching — optional and off by default: links copied in other apps open the add window right away (#793, #797)
- Close action — the close dialog has a "Remember my choice" option, and General settings sets what the close button does: ask, minimize to the tray or quit (#778)
- Drag files out — finished task cards drag their files to other apps and folders (#785)
- Remove missing records — a batch action removes only the records whose files no longer exist (#786)
- Quit from the floating window — its context menu has Quit (#794)
🛠 Improvements
- Lower CPU while downloading — progress bars animate on the compositor instead of re-laying out the window every frame, a visible task list updates only the cards that changed, and download history is built once per record instead of on every engine snapshot (#799, #791)
- Downloads through the engine — update packages and metadata, remote .torrent files, tracker lists, the BT blocklist and ED2K bootstrap lists are downloaded by the engine with multiple connections and the configured proxy; update packages are verified with the updater signature before install (#775)
- Retry from a new link — a failed task's Options page shows its source URL again, so it can retry from a replacement link and keep the data already received (#548, #769, #800)
- Subfolders in aria2 input — out=dir/name saves under that folder; absolute paths, .. and invalid names are refused with the offending value shown (#780)
- Proxy import — bypass rules the engine cannot use are skipped with an explanatory notice instead of a warning (#782)
- Linux GPU warning — the GPU acceleration switch warns on the NVIDIA proprietary driver, which freezes WebKitGTK, and diagnostics include the driver (#795)
- macOS requirement — the app declares macOS 11 as its minimum, so older systems get a clear message instead of a window that never appears (#805)
- Aria2 Next 3.1.0 — a task that failed before you quit comes back as failed instead of retrying at every launch (#802); a redirected download without a server-supplied name is saved under the final file name (#801); tracker tiers stay in order and unsupported trackers are skipped; servers that rotate entity tags keep multiple connections; the Windows engine supports long paths where the system enables them
🐛 Bug Fixes
- Fixed CPU and memory rising while the main window was hidden, with Web Content climbing towards a full core and 2 GB. Hidden and minimized windows no longer receive task snapshots and catch up when they return; the macOS Dock badge and progress bar redraw only when they change (#799, #791)
- Fixed the app freezing when quitting from the tray or Dock (#774)
- Fixed a browser handoff that failed on the original link not trying the URL the browser landed on, for example after a 403 (#790)
- Fixed switching task list tabs briefly showing the previous tab's cards (#781)
- Fixed the add window growing abruptly when opened with a torrent file, and the form emptying while the window closes
- Fixed Linux link handlers: portable builds no longer hide the installed app's menu entry, and package installs started by a browser running as an AppImage no longer take that browser for Rayburst (rayburst-connect#106)

zh-CN.description: 重新定义开源下载管理器
zh-CN.longDescription:
重新定义开源下载管理器

设计与动效
每个过渡和微交互均经过精心调优，严格遵循 Material Design 3 动效指南：
- 非对称时序 —— 入场动画略长于出场动画，让新内容有充分的时间呈现，同时让退出内容迅速离开
- 强调缓动曲线 —— 入场减速 (cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1))，出场加速 (cubic-bezier(0.3, 0, 0.8, 0.15))，在整个代码库中取代常规缓动曲线
- 基于弹簧模型的模态框 —— 对话框采用基于物理模型的弹簧动效，带来自然、灵敏的交互体验
- 一致的动效令牌 —— 所有时长和曲线均定义为 CSS 自定义属性，确保 12+ 个组件拥有统一的节奏

功能特性
- 多协议下载 —— HTTP、HTTPS、SFTP、ED2K、BitTorrent、Magnet 和 .torrent 任务
- HLS 与 DASH —— 原生音轨选择、字幕、直播录制、媒体断点续传以及 MP4/MKV 格式导出。详见媒体下载。
- BitTorrent —— 选择性文件下载、DHT、节点交换 (PEX)、加密控制、元数据缓存、GeoIP 节点国旗显示以及 Tracker 探测
- 浏览器扩展集成 —— 内嵌具备独立认证的扩展 API，支持下载确认、智能自动提交、文件名提示、Referer/Cookie 转发及实时控制 (Rayburst Connect)
- 安全的文件名处理 —— 支持 Content-Disposition、RFC 2047、非 UTF-8、百分号编码以及无后缀 URL 的解析，并具备路径遍历清理防护
- 下载整理 —— 收藏与常用文件夹、可选的文件类型分类、失效记录清理，以及基于 SQLite 的已完成历史记录
- 并发下载 —— 针对活动任务、连接流和 BitTorrent 节点分别提供独立的上限控制
- 速度控制 —— 全局及单任务上传/下载限速，支持按星期和具体时段设置调度计划
- 系统集成 —— 托盘操作、可选托盘网速显示、macOS Dock 标记/进度条，以及 magnet://、ed2k://、thunder:// 和 rayburst:// 的协议关联处理
- 轻量模式 —— 最小化到托盘时销毁 WebView，同时 Rust 保持核心引擎、任务监控、通知、历史记录和扩展路由持续运行
- 通知与电源选项 —— 原生任务开始/完成/失败通知、下载期间防止系统休眠，以及可选的下载完成后关机
- 网络控制 —— 支持对下载、应用更新和 Tracker 更新分作用域配置代理，并具备系统代理检测功能
- 自动更新通道 —— 提供 Stable、Beta 和跨通道最新策略，下载与安装阶段相互独立
- 诊断 —— 结构化日志、可导出的诊断 ZIP 包、数据库完整性检查以及 Linux GPU 渲染回退支持
- 个性化 —— 浅色/深色/跟随系统主题、10 种配色方案、27 种语言，以及首次启动检测系统语言
- 原生桌面应用 —— 基于 Tauri 2 与 Rust 后端构建
